newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER ADMITS CHAMPIONSHIP IS IN SIGHT.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER ADMITS CHAMPIONSHIP IS IN SIGHT.

text.p: Michael Schumacher finally admitted after his comfortable victory in the French Grand Prix that he could win this season's world drivers' championship.

After weeks of playing down his chances, Schumacher said he began to think about the possibility during Sunday's race as his Ferrari cruised home ahead of fellow German Heinz-Harald Frentzen in a Williams.
"It is possible because there are a few races ahead which will favour us," he said. "But I have not thought seriously about it -- I know it is going to be tough."

His supreme performance in outclassing the rest of the field at Magny-Cours endorsed the opinion that he was on his way to his third world title in four years, ending Ferrari's long 18-year drought without success in the drivers' championship.
If he does, it will be a timely return to success because Ferrari are celebrating their 50th birthday this year and have put together a formidable team for the future.
Frenchman Jean Todt, who has now completed four years with the team as sporting director, deserves much of the credit for the patient manner in which he has worked.

Todt, who enjoyed great success with Peugeot in rallying and sportscar racing, switched to Formula One with ease and his supreme professionalism, calm manner and eye for detail has set the tone which has helped lay the foundations of Ferrari's revival.
The arrivals of Schumacher, in 1996, and of technical director Ross Brawn, early this year, have completed the line-up. But Todt is still not certain that success is on its way.
"I worry about every day, every job and every race and it is the same with me until it is over...and then I begin to worry about the next one," he said.

"We have done a lot of good work and, of course, we have Michael Schumacher, who is a wonderful driver. But there is still a lot of work to do. I think Silverstone and the British Grand Prix will be difficult for us but we will go there to do our best."
While Ferrari have emerged as the new force, it has been a different story for pre-season favourite Williams and their Canadian driver Jacques Villeneuve.
Although Frentzen finished a strong second to Schumacher on Sunday, Villeneuve was fourth behind Briton Eddie Irvine in the second Ferrari and he now lies 14 points behind in the title race.
However, Villeneuve and Williams technical director Patrick Head remained stoical.
"This is just one race," said Head. "In this sport, as I know, it is all about heroes and villains from one week to the next.

"We accept that and we will go to Silverstone to test this week to improve things. Ferrari clearly outperformed us all round in this race and it is going to be a fierce battle for the championship this year."
